acceptance_criteria.evidence: The provisioning CLI provisions FACT / FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY / POLICY for one Issue with its six EVIDENCE/VERIFIER antecedents and is covered by 7 new tests (happy path resolves through resolve_pre_model_source_handling at the runtime boundary; exact rerun idempotent; authority mismatch fails closed; existing-but-mismatched authority head fails before any provenance write; provenance mismatch fails closed; as-of predating the rule or the Issue update fails closed; operator env guard; dual-source mutual exclusion). The bootstrap mutual-exclusion fix has 2 new tests (unit ValueError + CLI SystemExit with fresh DB untouched). The Railway deployment doc now lists steps (a)-(g) in the mandated order.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Live Railway Issue E2E is unblocked by the provisioned authority (verified via the runtime pre-model resolution boundary in tests).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_provisioning_publishes_exact_authority_records_for_one_issue provisions a fresh database through the CLI and then resolves the exact issue document identity with resolve_pre_model_source_handling at cutoff = updated_at + 1 day: fact_record.id, registry_record.id, decision.retention_decision == ALLOW, decision.field_category_registry_id == registry:<document_id>:v1, and authorization_rule.id == the genesis rule record id; provenance antecedents verified by the production resolver.

defect_families.evidence: DFF-007 swept on the provisioning path: every derived record scope is bound to issue_agent_document_id(authorization) (github-issue:repo#N) and the two registry/policy scopes derive from that exact id; the rule id is the genesis record id via bootstrap._expected_genesis_record_id, never a caller-supplied rule string; the operator environment guard (EVIDENCE_DATABASE_ENV/VERIFICATION_KEY/SHA/GENESIS_RULE_SHA256) must match this exact bootstrap and signing key, or the run fails closed before any write. test_provisioning_requires_operator_environment_configuration pins the guard; the happy path asserts the exact canonical (family, scope) keys.

DFF-008 swept: record ids are content-addressed and derived byte-for-byte as the repository service derives them (sha256 of _canonical_json(_plain_mapping(payload)) for authority records via _publish; sha256 of the provenance claims payload for provenance records), and _provision_authority_record re-verifies the published result.record_id equals the derived id, so a forgery or a service deviation is structurally detectable and blocks the success report. Provenance exact-head pre-check computes the would-be id and refuses to supersede a different head.

DFF-009 swept: the CLI itself raised an unsatisfiable proof obligation on the first end-to-end attempt - records claimed known_at = issue_updated_at (a past instant) while physical admission is wall-clock now, so the authority publication's provenance-antecedent validation found the EVIDENCE/VERIFIER antecedents not strict-known at the authority known_at ('canonical publication provenance is incomplete', SystemExit 2). Resolved by the explicit --as-of operator instant and the authority-time clamp authority_at = max(as_of, max provenance admission), which is a deterministic function of the pinned as-of. The happy path now issues all three authorizations and consumes them, with exactly six provenance records present.

DFF-010 swept: bootstrap's _load_signing_key silently preferred the file over the environment and never errored; now both sources together raise an explicit deterministic ValueError before any database is opened (the raise precedes the database argument parsing path). test_signing_key_sources_are_mutually_exclusive (unit) and test_both_signing_key_sources_fail_closed_before_db_open (CLI, asserts the fresh database is not created) pin both success and fail-closed shapes. The provisioning CLI consumes the same shared loader and gains the same mutual-exclusion property via test_provisioning_signing_key_sources_are_mutually_exclusive. The authority-head exact pre-check likewise enforces prevention at the earliest boundary: it fails closed before any provenance or authority write, not merely by detecting a mismatch after mutation.

DFF-011 swept: nothing in this candidate makes a valid commit permanently inadmissible. The as-of guards reject an as-of predating the genesis rule (clear error), predating the Issue's updated_at, and -- after normalization, immediately and before the provenance repository is constructed or any provenance/authority write occurs -- a FUTURE as-of ('the provisioning as-of must not be in the future'); the redundant later future check was removed. test_provisioning_refuses_future_as_of_before_any_mutation leaves the database with only the genesis/canonical state: zero per-Issue provenance records and heads, zero FACT/FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY/POLICY authority records, unchanged canonical keys and operator root.

DFF-012 swept: the provisioning CLI mints no connector authorization receipts and introduces no receipt-freshness path; the only new persisted writes are the provenance/authority records through the repository service, and connector receipt freshness over the pushed range remains enforced by the repository-local push boundary. No receipt-driven admission logic is added or changed.

DFF-013 swept: this pre-ready hostile review is being recorded for the exact candidate head (base 8c26e09, head bf68e8c) via scripts/hunter_pre_ready_review.py --record --issue 430 and verified with the same base/head arguments before push; the review covers all ten applicable families and the four Issue acceptance bullets.

DFF-014 swept: idempotency is exact-match only. On a re-run pinned to the recorded as_of, every would-be provenance id and authority record id equals the current head, so nothing is written (test_provisioning_exact_rerun_is_idempotent asserts byte-stable canonical keys, revision 1, identical record counts). Any other authority content (test_provisioning_mismatched_authority_content_fails_closed, sensitivity RESTRICTED) fails closed before write with 'refusing to replace provisioned authority state', and a mismatched existing authority head is now detected and rejected before ANY provenance write (test_provisioning_mismatched_authority_head_fails_before_any_provenance_write: existing FACT head + zero per-Issue provenance, then SystemExit 2, zero provenance/authority writes, canonical keys and record counts unchanged). A different provenance head also fails closed before any write. The printed as_of is the pinned, deterministic operator instant - not a fresh transient each run.

DFF-015 swept: the mutual-exclusion guard is enforced at the earliest practical boundary - the shared _load_signing_key raises before the database path is even read, not merely detected by a later check; the regression test proves a fresh DB is untouched. The provisioning config guard (DFF-009-adjacent) also fails before any write. These are prevention-by-construction at entry, not detection-only.

DFF-016 swept: each FACT / FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY / POLICY issuance names its own EVIDENCE and VERIFIER identity, and all six provenance records are written before the first issuance; the authority-time clamp keeps known_at at or after the highest provenance admission so each record remains resolvable at its own known_at, and the clamp is a deterministic function of the pinned as-of so the exact re-run reproduces identical records without removing or duplicating proof. No proof is ever dropped to shorten a path.

findings.evidence: The provisioning CLI wrote the six EVIDENCE/VERIFIER provenance records before checking whether existing FACT / FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY / POLICY authority heads exactly matched the would-be records, so a run against an existing-but-mismatched authority head mutated provenance before rejecting the authority. Resolved by deriving the expected record id for all three authority families, reading each current canonical head through the repository resolver store (current_canonical_head_id), and failing closed before any provenance write on the first mismatch; exact-match heads remain on the idempotent path. New regression test pins zero provenance/authority writes and unchanged canonical state.

Backdating the per-Issue records to issue_updated_at is impossible in this contract: authority records' claimed known_at must be at or after their physical admission, and an Issue classified 'now' cannot be knowable before its last update. The first end-to-end run failed with 'canonical publication provenance is incomplete' (SystemExit 2) because the EVIDENCE/VERIFIER antecedents were admitted later than the authority records' known_at. Resolved with the explicit operator --as-of instant and the clamp authority_at = max(as_of, max provenance admission), itself a deterministic function of the pinned as-of. Happy path green; exact rerun idempotent.

A future --as-of could previously reach provenance writes before the redundant future-time check that sat later in the write path, violating fail-closed-before-mutation. Resolved by moving the future as-of rejection to immediately after on_or_after is parsed and normalized, before the provenance repository is constructed and before any provenance/authority write, and removing the later redundant check. New regression test (fresh bootstrapped DB + future --as-of) pins exit 2 with zero per-Issue provenance records, zero FACT/FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY/POLICY authority records, and unchanged genesis/root and canonical state.

The exact-head provenance pre-check queried source_handling_provenance_heads before the provenance schema existed on a fresh database, failing with sqlite3.OperationalError 'no such table'. Resolved by constructing SourceHandlingProvenanceAuthorityRepository (whose initializer creates the schema idempotently) before running the head pre-check. The fresh-database happy path now passes.

bootstrap_source_handling_authority._load_signing_key silently preferred --signing-key-file over HUNTER_SOURCE_HANDLING_SIGNING_KEY and never errored, so a misconfigured operator could be masking a stale env value. Resolved: both sources together raise an explicit deterministic ValueError before any database is opened; the provisioning CLI inherits the same loader. Unit and CLI-level tests pin the pre-DB fail-closed.

Two racing provisioning processes on the same empty database both observe absent heads; the second writer's provenance writes then no-op or supersede depending on content, while the authority issue_authorization/publish path has its own genesis-style guards. Safe and fail-closed in both orders, but the graceful classification of the loser as already-provisioned is left to a follow-up rather than implemented here.

Classification content (sensitivity, restrictions, dispositions) comes from operator-supplied options, not from reading the live Issue content; a real-content verification step remains the operator's responsibility (the command fails closed on a missing document contract rather than inventing content). Accepted for this operator-only provisioning path.
